title: eMudhra intermediate CA private keys recoverable from the certificates
summary: Eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs, sixteen certificates including Sectigo AAA cross-signs, were issued with keys that anyone can recover from the certificates themselves. Whoever holds a key can mint TLS or code-signing certificates for any name that chains to those intermediates. Browsers block them through revocation lists, but most non-browser clients (curl, package managers, language runtimes, Java, Node, Electron apps) check neither revocation nor Certificate Transparency, so any trust store that still carries one of the four anchoring roots, and has no distrust record for the intermediates, accepts forged certificates.

sources.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise (Dennis Jackson and contributors)

applicability.summary: Any machine, container image or runtime that carries a CA trust store: Linux, macOS, Windows or BSD, plus every bundled copy in Python, Java, Node, Go, Rust and desktop applications
conditions: The host or an application on it makes TLS connections or verifies code signatures using a trust store it carries itself.
That store still contains one of the four anchor roots and has no distrust record for the sixteen compromised certificates.
The client using that store does not check revocation (OCSP, CRL, OneCRL, CRLSets, CRLite) and does not enforce Certificate Transparency, which is true of almost every non-browser client.

indicators.name: emSign Root TLS CA - G3
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: Direct issuer of the six compromised TLS intermediates. Present in a store without a distrust record for the intermediates means that store validates forged TLS certificates. Included by Microsoft; not in the Mozilla, Apple or Chrome root programs.

indicators.name: emSign Root CS CA - G3
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: Direct issuer of the two compromised code-signing intermediates. Present in a store used for signature verification means that store accepts forged code signatures. Included by Microsoft only.

indicators.name: AAA Certificate Services
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: Cross-signs all eight compromised intermediates. Present in a store without a distrust record means the store validates forged certificates via the cross-signed path. This root is in every major root program and many legitimate sites chain to it, so removing it has side effects.

indicators.name: emSign ECC Root CA - G3
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: Cross-signs emSign Root TLS CA - G3, so chains anchored here also validate. Present in a store without a distrust record means the store validates forged TLS certificates. In every major root program; this is the root most Linux bundles and certifi carried.

indicators.name: EM DV TLS CA - G3B
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate (eMudhra-issued and Sectigo cross-signed certificates). Present as a trusted certificate means the store trusts it directly; present in a distrust or blocked list means the store has the fix for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM OV TLS CA - G3B
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate. Present as trusted means direct trust; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM EV TLS CA - G3B
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate. Present as trusted means direct trust; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM DV TLS CA - G3C
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate. Present as trusted means direct trust; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM OV TLS CA - G3C
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate. Present as trusted means direct trust; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM EV TLS CA - G3C
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised intermediate. Present as trusted means direct trust; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM OV CS CA - G3B
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised code-signing intermediate. Present as trusted means the store accepts forged code signatures through it; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: EM OV CS CA - G3C
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: A compromised code-signing intermediate. Present as trusted means the store accepts forged code signatures through it; present in a distrust list means the fix is in place for that certificate.

indicators.name: emSign Root TLS CA - G3 (cross-signed by emSign ECC Root CA - G3)
indicators.comparison: sha256 of the DER certificate, case-insensitive; SKI is a secondary key for stores that expose it
indicators.meaning: The cross-sign that lets chains to emSign Root TLS CA - G3 validate under emSign ECC Root CA - G3. Its key is not itself leaked; it is listed because a store that pins or blocks by this certificate must include it. Present in a distrust list means the cross-signed path is blocked.

indicators.backport_note: Each distribution keys the fix on its own package version; compare with the distribution's comparator (dpkg --compare-versions, rpm, apk) and never with the Mozilla NSS version the package was derived from. RHEL 7 and Bottlerocket had no fixed version on the source's table as of as_of.
indicators.meaning: Package version at or above the floor for that distribution establishes that the shipped bundle no longer carries the anchor roots. It says nothing about a bundle edited locally, a bundle in a container image, or any other store on the host; read the bundle itself where you can.

indicators.product: Root store bundles and libraries (certifi, NSS, curl CA bundle, rustls-webpki, webpki-roots, Mozilla::CA, Composer ca-bundle, Erlang certifi, Elixir castore, CFSSL)
indicators.backport_note: certifi on Debian and Ubuntu is patched to return the system bundle path, so its own cacert.pem file may be present and unused; report which file the interpreter actually resolves. Rust and Go roots are compiled into each binary, so the floor applies per binary, not per host.
indicators.meaning: Library version at or above the floor establishes that the library's shipped bundle no longer carries the anchor roots. For compiled-in stores (Rust, Go, Electron) this is the only evidence available and the report must say so.

indicators.product: Language runtimes with a compiled-in or bundled store (Node.js, Bun, Deno, Electron, Go, Java, Python)

affected.fixed: 3.15.1, 3.14.9, 3.13.17 (Python; applies to the bundled certifi in python.org and Windows Store builds)

indicators.backport_note: Distribution JDK packages (Debian openjdk-21-jre-headless, RHEL java-21-openjdk) carry their own version numbers and may regenerate cacerts from the system bundle at install time; read the keystore rather than trusting the version. Node on Linux uses its compiled-in store unless NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca or NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS changes that.
indicators.meaning: Runtime version at or above the floor for its major establishes that the runtime's own store no longer carries the anchor roots. A runtime below the floor whose store can be read (Java cacerts, Node rootCertificates) should be read; the store finding wins over the version.

indicators.product: Applications and tools that ship their own store (ArgoCD, Claude Code, Conda, Docker Desktop, Git for Windows, mise, Obsidian, pip, pixi, pypi-publish action, Rustup, uv, Visual Studio Code)
indicators.backport_note: Godot had no fixed version on the source's table as of as_of. pip's vendored certifi is separate from the certifi package in the same environment; both need checking.
indicators.meaning: Application version at or above the floor establishes that the application's own bundled store no longer carries the anchor roots. Most of these stores cannot be read directly, so the version is the only evidence and the report says so.

coverage.store: Other bundled and compiled-in stores (curl bundle, Go, Rust, Electron apps, Claude Code, VS Code, Docker Desktop, Git for Windows, pip, uv, conda, rustup, mise, pixi)

locations: each application's own files; mostly not readable as PEM
platforms.note: version evidence only. Required only for applications that are installed; the agent lists what it found and what it did not look for

limitations: A store that contains an anchor is reported affected for clients that do not check revocation. A client that does check CRL or OCSP, or enforces Certificate Transparency, is protected despite the finding; the advisory cannot tell which clients those are.

Container images, virtual machines and remote hosts each carry their own stores and are not reached by commands run on this host. The agent lists images it can see as a gap unless the user runs the same read-only commands inside them.
Compiled-in stores (Go, Rust, Electron, Bun, Deno, most desktop applications) cannot be read; only the version floor applies and the report says so.
The patch-status floors were copied from the reference page on as_of and have no revision date of their own; a newer page may list more products or different versions.
Matching is by certificate SHA-256 and, where a store exposes it, SKI. Stores that show only SHA-1 thumbprints (Windows certutil default output) need the PowerShell block that computes SHA-256.

uncheckable.why: no command from this host reads a phone's system trust store or its Play services block list
uncheckable.user_should: open Settings, search Trusted credentials, System tab, and confirm emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services are disabled or that the device has received the block; some vendors (HarmonyOS) do not allow disabling system roots

uncheckable.what: Whether browsers on this machine received the block lists
uncheckable.why: OneCRL, CRLSets and CRLite state is inside each browser profile and is not exposed as a file this advisory can match
uncheckable.user_should: keep the browser updated; the reference site's in-browser checker and the opt-in live check show whether this browser still accepts the chains

uncheckable.what: Whether Windows received the automatic certificate trust list update
uncheckable.why: the update populates the Disallowed store, which the Windows check reads, but a machine that is offline or has updates disabled shows the same empty Disallowed store as one that was never affected
uncheckable.user_should: run the Windows check and, if the compromised certificates are absent from Disallowed, treat the anchors as trusted

uncheckable.what: Applications that pin or embed certificates in their own format
uncheckable.user_should: check the vendor's advisory and the version floors in fix.md

remediation.summary: Upgrade the package or runtime that ships each affected store to the floor in the indicators; that is the durable fix. Where no fixed version exists yet, distrust the two Mozilla-program roots (emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services) in the system store using the platform's blocklist mechanism, keeping the reference site's warnings: not for ordinary users on Linux, not for enterprise-managed Windows devices. Then re-run the check.

live_check.privacy: Quoted from the source: "The servers behind the checker record how many times each user-agent connects successfully, meaning it still trusts the compromised intermediates. Only these counts are recorded." A JSON dump with counts per JA4 fingerprint is also published.

hosts.proves: a successful TLS connection means this client trusts the compromised EM DV TLS CA - G3B via emSign Root TLS CA - G3 or its cross-sign
hosts.negative_means: a certificate error means this client, with the store it actually uses, does not trust that chain; it says nothing about other clients or stores on the host

hosts.proves: a successful TLS connection means this client trusts the compromised intermediate via the Sectigo AAA cross-sign
hosts.negative_means: a certificate error means this client does not trust that chain

hosts.proves: the leaf was never logged to Certificate Transparency: success means this client trusts the intermediate and does not enforce CT, which is the client an attacker can hit without anyone noticing
hosts.negative_means: a certificate error means either the intermediate is not trusted or CT is enforced; compare with the host above to tell which

hosts.proves: same as the no-CT test, via the AAA cross-sign
